text:
acme_prod: Hey @jess_support — after we switched our embedding provider to rwd-embed-small-v2, our rerank endpoint started returning absurdly high scores for unrelated docs (0.99+). No HTTP errors, call succeeds. sample req id: req-3b2f. Can someone triage?

jess_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact rerank request (sanitized) and the embedding model(s) you used to generate vectors? Also the rerank model name.

acme_prod: Pasting sanitized payload: 
```json
{
  "reranker": "rwd-rerank-base-v1",
  "queries": ["what's our refund policy?"],
  "candidate_embeddings": [ [ /* base64 redacted */ ], /* 120 docs */ ],
  "embedded_source": "rwd-embed-small-v2"
}
```
Note: the embedding arrays are produced by the new vendor and each vector len is 1536 per our client logs. Previously we used vectors sized 1024.

mike_eng: tagging @anya_ml and @priya_sre. If vectors are different sizes the reranker should either reject or handle gracefully. Are you sending the embedding model metadata in the rerank call, or only raw vectors?

acme_prod: Only raw vectors so far — we assumed rerank would be agnostic. The SDK path we use is a two-step flow: generate embeddings separately, then call /rerank with those arrays.

anya_ml: This is expected behavior when mixing embed sources without metadata. Our reranker implementation currently assumes a configured default embedding dim for the customer (1024) and does not validate per-request vector length. If the request sends 1536-length vectors, the scoring math will still run but the extra tail dims get ignored/truncated in the internal dot-product window, producing nondeterministic high scores.

anya_ml: Quick repro steps I used: 
```python
# simplified repro
from math import sqrt
q = [0.1]*1536
d = [0.1]*1024 + [0.0]*512  # older doc vectors padded to 1536 on ingestion
# internal dot product computed over first 1024 dims only -> misleading similarity
```

jess_support: @acme_prod can you confirm whether your document store still has 1024-dim vectors (older docs) while the new query embeddings are 1536? That would explain mismatches.

acme_prod: Yes — docs were indexed months ago with the old embed model (1024). New queries use rwd-embed-small-v2 (1536). We didn't reindex docs.

mike_eng: Ok that explains it. Short-term mitigations: 1) stop sending new 1536-length query vectors and revert to the prior embedding model, or 2) reindex docs with 1536 embeddings.

anya_ml: Engineering action items I recommend: 
- Reject rerank requests where any vector length != customer's configured dimension (return 400 + clear message).
- Add an opt-in compatibility pad/truncate mode for customers who want automatic behavior (explicit flag).
- Emit a warning header when embedding_dim mismatches are detected (X-Embed-Dim-Expected, X-Embed-Dim-Received).

priya_sre: I'll run a quick search across logs for other customers sending inconsistent dims. If we see a spike, we can fire a high-priority pager.

tom_cs: I'll draft a short note to customers who have recently changed embedding providers and may be affected, include recommended actions above.

mike_eng: I'll put a small hotfix PR up to add the dimension validation and the warning header. Plan: return 400 by default when mismatched, and add `compatibility_mode` flag to allow auto pad/truncate. Canary deploy in 30m.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for service rerank-scorer (canary id: can-879).

mike_eng: Canary passed basic checks, rolling to 10% now. Validation endpoint: `POST /v1/rerank` will now return 400 + body: `{\"error\":\"embedding_dim_mismatch\",\"expected\":1024,\"received\":1536}` if dims disagree.

acme_prod: Thanks everyone — we'll either revert our client to the old embed model for now or start reindexing. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

jess_support: Closing loop — note: @acme_prod please share the request id if you see the 400 after the patch so we can confirm. We'll follow up once we identify other affected customers. :thumbsup:
